name: Baga Koga
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Relich, Randa Rae 1973 'General grammar of Koba Baga with texts and translations'

sources.citation: Lamp, Frederick John. 2021. Baga Tshi-Tem Dictionary (Guinea). PDF, Cataloging Africana.
sources.note: Contains a handful of 'Bkb = Baga Koba' entries and says 'no dictionaries exist for these dialects'; its initial-accent remark concerns Baga Sitemu (bsp), not Koba.

sources.citation: Rochant, Neige. 2023. A bilectal grammar of Baga Pukur: an Atlantic language of Guinea. PhD thesis, Universite Sorbonne Nouvelle. p. 229.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Second-hand, about the Baga (Mel) group generally, not Koga specifically: "neighbouring Mel languages along the coast, such as the Baga group, are not known to be tonal." Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Moran, Steven, McCloy, Daniel & Wright, Richard. PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory PH 1060 'Baga Koga; Koba; Barka', source Relich 1973.
sources.note: Segment inventory only (25 segments); no tone segments and nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Grambank language page baga1273 (coder Soeren Pieper; sources Houis 1953, Relich 1973).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; useful only as evidence that Relich 1973 is in library circulation.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund W. 1854. Polyglotta Africana. London: Church Missionary House. (archive.org id polyglottaafrica00koel, scanned text). Baga = Kalum-Baga of Balanser opposite the Isles de Los.
sources.note: Wordlist with accent marks only; the introduction states "' the common sign for the accent, e.g., a, d" (scanned) and gives no rule for where the accent falls in Baga.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Baga language' (en); fr.wikipedia has no article.
sources.note: No phonological information; cites Wilson 1962, Wilson 2007, Fields-Black 2008.

sources.citation: Relich, Randa Rae. 1973. A general grammar of Koba Baga with texts and translations (Mel, French Guinea). MA thesis, Duquesne University, 44 pp. ProQuest 1304569; OCLC 64151052.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: The only descriptive grammar of Baga Koga on record (Glottolog grammar sketch; PHOIBLE and Grambank both coded from it), so its phonology section is the one place a stress/tone statement for this language is likely to exist.

sources.citation: Wilson, William Andre Auquier. 2007. Guinea Languages of the Atlantic Group: description and internal classification. Schriften zur Afrikanistik 12. Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang. ISBN 9783631557686.

sources.note: Wilson's own 1950s-60s field data on Baga Koba, Sitemu and Maduri, written up in ch. 9 'Temne and the Baga languages' with a tone section (9.2.3); the best chance of a first-hand prosodic remark on Baga Koba by a linguist.
